findings.evidence: Line 132: `price = float(product.price) if product.price else 0` — Decimal-to-float cast in serialization. Also line 133: `compare_price = float(product.compare_price) if product.compare_price else None`, line 346: `rating=float(data.pop("rating", 0.0) or 0.0)`, line 727: `product.compare_price = float(compare_price) if compare_price else None`, line 752: `product.compare_price = float(payload["compare_price"]) if payload["compare_price"] else None`
findings.notes: Confirmed: multiple float() casts on monetary fields (price, compare_price) throughout the service. Law 19 explicitly forbids float for money — 'Monetary values MUST use Decimal or Numeric. Float FORBIDDEN for money.' The serialization path (lines 132-133) is especially problematic because it drops precision before the value leaves the backend.

findings.evidence: Line 305: `products = ordered.offset(offset).limit(limit).all()` — OFFSET pagination on customer product listing. Lines 287-303 show a cursor-based pagination path exists but is only used when the `cursor` parameter is provided; the default path falls through to OFFSET.
findings.notes: Confirmed: OFFSET is still the default pagination mechanism for the hottest path (customer product listing). Law 317 states 'NEVER OFFSET on hot lists'. A keyset cursor path exists (lines 287-303) but is not wired as the default, making this a valid performance finding.

findings.evidence: Line 248: `q_obj = q_obj.filter(Product.name.ilike(f"%{q}%"))` — leading wildcard ILIKE with no GIN/pg_trgm support. The Product model (lines 42-48) defines B-tree indexes on supplier_id, category, created_at, and country_code but no GIN index on `name`.
findings.notes: Confirmed: leading wildcard `%q%` forces sequential scan on products table. TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md §2 states pg_trgm is a built-in PG 18 feature for fuzzy search, but it is not utilized here. A GIN index on catalog.products.name using pg_trgm would allow the ILIKE to use an index.
